::: {#thm-de-morgan-logic}
#### De Morgan's laws

For propositions $P$ and $Q$
[@wikipedia_de_morgans_laws]:

1. $\neg (P \land Q) \equiv \neg P \lor \neg Q$;
2. $\neg (P \lor Q) \equiv \neg P \land \neg Q$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

For law 1, the fourth and last columns of this table match in every row:

| $P$ | $Q$ | $P \land Q$ | $\neg (P \land Q)$ | $\neg P$ | $\neg Q$ | $\neg P \lor \neg Q$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| T | T | T | F | F | F | F |
| T | F | F | T | F | T | T |
| F | T | F | T | T | F | T |
| F | F | F | T | T | T | T |

Law 2 follows from law 1.
Law 1 holds for any two propositions, so it holds for $\neg P$ and $\neg Q$:
$$
\neg (\neg P \land \neg Q) \equiv \neg \neg P \lor \neg \neg Q.
$$
By double negation (@thm-double-negation) and @thm-substitution,
the right side is logically equivalent to $P \lor Q$, so
$$
\neg (\neg P \land \neg Q) \equiv P \lor Q.
$$
Negating both sides (@thm-substitution) gives
$$
\neg \neg (\neg P \land \neg Q) \equiv \neg (P \lor Q),
$$
and by double negation the left side is logically equivalent to $\neg P \land \neg Q$.
So $\neg (P \lor Q) \equiv \neg P \land \neg Q$.

:::

:::
